headline: The hamlet on the lip of the well now has streets
lede: TEN-DEEP's surface world stops being a menu: THE RIM is a two-lane cobbled hamlet you walk tile by tile — hedges and the well curb block the way, every door must be reached on foot, and the sim remembers exactly where the company stands.

notes.text: Walk law: arrows step the hero, refused steps book a walkBlocked event (an unmoving frame is an answer), SPACE crosses only the threshold you stand on, and leaving a shop steps you onto its own doorstep.
Determinism untouched: the street map is fixed data, the proofs bypass the town, and stateHash now rides the hero's tile — replays pin every step.
tendeepcheck gained 8 street-law gates (968/968) and two proven mutants: kill the blocked() lane lookup and the hedges become decor; kill the threshold guard and doors open from across the road.

Slot b's first claim of the night was refused (slot a shipped FireCrew's wind cue mid-session), the flagship gaps all proved CLOSED, so the never-dry rung put TEN-DEEP's oldest honest gap on the board — filed #1751, shipped #1754, polish pass #1756 filed for QA.

look.text: Walk THE RIM: arrows stroll, the hedges say no, the well glows at your back
